correctness.rationale: The two rim families and two cross families form C_(2n)^2, counted once even at n=3. The side-triangle incidence bound in RESULT.md gives F>=n+(r_a+r_b)/2, with each rim defect count congruent to n modulo 2. An independent check uses bonds e_i=sigma_i sigma_(i+1) on the squared ring. If p is the number of + bonds and q the number of their cyclic runs in a nonconstant bond sequence, the energy in units J is 2p-4q, p is even, and q<=min(p,2n-p). The constant bond sequences cannot minimize. For even n, the minimum requires p=q=n, giving two alternating bond sequences and two spin orientations per sequence, each with M=0. For odd n, the minimum requires p=q=n-1: at p>=n+1 the bound gives energy at least -2n+6, and at p<=n-3 it gives at least -2n+6. The minimizing spin sequences have n+1 alternating-sign spin runs, exactly two of length 1 and all others length 2. To count labelled sequences, choose one of 2n start sites, a starting spin and the two short runs, and divide by n+1 possible choices of marked run. The two short runs on opposite signs give M=0 and count n(n+1); placing both on one sign gives n(n-1)/2 for each M=+2 and -2. Finite Gibbs fluctuation-response gives k_B T chi=Var(M), tending to the stated equal-weight ground variance at fixed n. A separate exhaustive squared-cycle enumeration for 3<=n<=9 reproduced the energy minima and each magnetization sector; it does not prove larger n. The uploaded checker was not executed.
